For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }

Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

"""kitty: track shared expenses on group trips and work out who owes whom."""
import sys

from kitty.cli import main

sys.exit(main())
"""Command-line interface: python3 -m kitty <command>."""
import argparse
import csv
import datetime
import json
import sys
from decimal import Decimal

from kitty import ledger, store
from kitty.errors import KittyError
from kitty.money import (
    allocate,
    fmt,
    parse_amount,
    parse_currency,
    parse_date,
    parse_rate,
    parse_weight,
    to_cents,
)


class Parser(argparse.ArgumentParser):
    """An ArgumentParser that exits with status 1 on usage errors."""

    def error(self, message):
        self.print_usage(sys.stderr)
        self.exit(1, f"{self.prog}: error: {message}\n")


def output(value):
    print(json.dumps(value, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))


# --- validation helpers -------------------------------------------------------

def require_member(data, name):
    name = name.strip()
    if name not in data["members"]:
        raise KittyError(f"unknown member: {name!r}")
    return name


def check_unique(names, option):
    seen = set()
    for name in names:
        if name in seen:
            raise KittyError(f"{option} lists {name!r} more than once")
        seen.add(name)


def parse_pairs(data, text, option, parse_value):
    """Parse "A=30,B=20" into [(name, value), ...]."""
    pairs = []
    for item in text.split(","):
        name, sep, value = item.partition("=")
        if not sep or not name.strip() or not value.strip():
            raise KittyError(f"{option} expects NAME=VALUE pairs separated by commas, got {item!r}")
        pairs.append((require_member(data, name), parse_value(value, f"{option} value for {name.strip()}")))
    check_unique([name for name, _ in pairs], option)
    return pairs


def rate_for(data, currency):
    if currency == data["base_currency"]:
        return Decimal(1)
    if currency not in data["rates"]:
        raise KittyError(
            f"no exchange rate for {currency}; set one with 'python3 -m kitty rate set {currency} RATE'"
        )
    return Decimal(data["rates"][currency])


def convert(data, amount, currency):
    rate = rate_for(data, currency)
    base_amount = to_cents(amount * rate)
    if base_amount == 0:
        raise KittyError(f"{fmt(amount)} {currency} is less than 0.01 {data['base_currency']}")
    return rate, base_amount


def split_weights(data, args, amount):
    chosen = [opt for opt in ("among", "exact", "shares", "percent") if getattr(args, opt) is not None]
    if len(chosen) > 1:
        raise KittyError("use only one of " + ", ".join(f"--{opt}" for opt in chosen))
    if args.exact is not None:
        pairs = parse_pairs(data, args.exact, "--exact", lambda v, w: parse_amount(v, w, allow_zero=True))
        total = sum(v for _, v in pairs)
        if total != amount:
            raise KittyError(f"--exact amounts add up to {fmt(total)} but the expense is {fmt(amount)}")
        return pairs
    if args.shares is not None:
        return parse_pairs(data, args.shares, "--shares", parse_weight)
    if args.percent is not None:
        pairs = parse_pairs(data, args.percent, "--percent", parse_weight)
        total = sum(v for _, v in pairs)
        if total != 100:
            raise KittyError(f"--percent values add up to {total.normalize():f}, not 100")
        return pairs
    if args.among is not None:
        names = [require_member(data, n) for n in args.among.split(",") if n.strip()]
        if not names:
            raise KittyError("--among needs at least one name")
        check_unique(names, "--among")
    else:
        names = list(data["members"])
    return [(name, Decimal(1)) for name in names]


# --- commands -----------------------------------------------------------------

def cmd_init(args):
    if store.exists():
        raise KittyError(f"{store.DATA_FILE} already exists here")
    currency = parse_currency(args.currency)
    store.save(store.new_kitty(currency))
    print(f"Started a new kitty in {currency}")


def cmd_member_add(args):
    data = store.load()
    name = args.name.strip()
    if not name:
        raise KittyError("member name must not be empty")
    if "," in name or "=" in name:
        raise KittyError("member names cannot contain ',' or '='")
    if name in data["members"]:
        raise KittyError(f"{name!r} is already a member")
    data["members"].append(name)
    store.save(data)
    print(f"Added {name}")


def cmd_member_remove(args):
    data = store.load()
    name = require_member(data, args.name)
    involved = any(name == e["payer"] or name in e["shares"] for e in data["expenses"]) or any(
        name in (p["from"], p["to"]) for p in data["payments"]
    )
    if involved:
        raise KittyError(f"cannot remove {name}: they appear in expenses or payments")
    data["members"].remove(name)
    store.save(data)
    print(f"Removed {name}")


def cmd_member_list(args):
    output(store.load()["members"])


def cmd_expense_add(args):
    data = store.load()
    payer = require_member(data, args.payer)
    amount = parse_amount(args.amount)
    description = " ".join(args.description).strip()
    if not description:
        raise KittyError("description must not be empty")
    currency = parse_currency(args.currency) if args.currency else data["base_currency"]
    date = parse_date(args.date) if args.date else datetime.date.today().isoformat()
    category = args.category.strip() if args.category is not None else "other"
    if not category:
        raise KittyError("category must not be empty")
    weights = split_weights(data, args, amount)
    if not weights:
        raise KittyError("there are no members to split the expense among; add some first")
    rate, base_amount = convert(data, amount, currency)
    shares = allocate(base_amount, weights)

    expense_id = data["next_id"]
    data["next_id"] += 1
    data["expenses"].append({
        "id": expense_id,
        "date": date,
        "payer": payer,
        "description": description,
        "amount": fmt(amount),
        "currency": currency,
        "rate": str(rate),
        "base_amount": fmt(base_amount),
        "category": category,
        "shares": {name: fmt(share) for name, share in shares.items()},
    })
    store.save(data)
    print(expense_id)


def expense_json(e):
    return {
        "id": e["id"],
        "date": e["date"],
        "payer": e["payer"],
        "description": e["description"],
        "amount": e["amount"],
        "currency": e["currency"],
        "base_amount": e["base_amount"],
        "category": e["category"],
        "shares": e["shares"],
    }


def cmd_expense_list(args):
    output([expense_json(e) for e in ledger.sorted_expenses(store.load())])


def cmd_expense_remove(args):
    data = store.load()
    try:
        expense_id = int(args.id)
    except ValueError:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid expense ID: {args.id!r}")
    remaining = [e for e in data["expenses"] if e["id"] != expense_id]
    if len(remaining) == len(data["expenses"]):
        raise KittyError(f"no expense with ID {expense_id}")
    data["expenses"] = remaining
    store.save(data)
    print(f"Removed expense {expense_id}")


def cmd_payment_add(args):
    data = store.load()
    sender = require_member(data, args.sender)
    recipient = require_member(data, args.recipient)
    if sender == recipient:
        raise KittyError("a payment needs two different people")
    amount = parse_amount(args.amount)
    currency = parse_currency(args.currency) if args.currency else data["base_currency"]
    date = parse_date(args.date) if args.date else datetime.date.today().isoformat()
    rate, base_amount = convert(data, amount, currency)
    data["payments"].append({
        "id": max((p["id"] for p in data["payments"]), default=0) + 1,
        "date": date,
        "from": sender,
        "to": recipient,
        "amount": fmt(amount),
        "currency": currency,
        "rate": str(rate),
        "base_amount": fmt(base_amount),
    })
    store.save(data)
    print(f"Recorded {sender} paying {recipient} {fmt(amount)} {currency}")


def cmd_rate_set(args):
    data = store.load()
    currency = parse_currency(args.currency)
    if currency == data["base_currency"]:
        raise KittyError(f"{currency} is the base currency; its rate is always 1")
    rate = parse_rate(args.rate)
    data["rates"][currency] = str(rate)
    store.save(data)
    print(f"1 {currency} = {rate} {data['base_currency']}")


def cmd_balances(args):
    output({name: fmt(v) for name, v in ledger.balances(store.load()).items()})


def cmd_settle(args):
    output([
        {"from": sender, "to": recipient, "amount": fmt(amount)}
        for sender, recipient, amount in ledger.settle(store.load())
    ])


def cmd_history(args):
    data = store.load()
    name = require_member(data, args.name)
    output([
        {"date": date, "description": description, "change": fmt(change), "balance": fmt(balance)}
        for date, description, change, balance in ledger.history(data, name)
    ])


def cmd_report(args):
    output({
        category: {name: fmt(v) for name, v in people.items()}
        for category, people in ledger.report(store.load()).items()
    })


def cmd_export(args):
    data = store.load()
    expenses = ledger.sorted_expenses(data)
    columns = ["id", "date", "payer", "description", "amount", "currency", "category", "base_amount"]
    try:
        with open(args.file, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=columns, extrasaction="ignore")
            writer.writeheader()

from decimal import Decimal


def sorted_expenses(data):
    return sorted(data["expenses"], key=lambda e: (e["date"], e["id"]))


def _events(data):
    """Expenses and payments in date order (ties in the order they were added)."""
    events = [(e["date"], 0, e["id"], "expense", e) for e in data["expenses"]]
    events += [(p["date"], 1, p["id"], "payment", p) for p in data["payments"]]
    events.sort(key=lambda ev: ev[:3])
    return [(kind, item) for *_, kind, item in events]


def balances(data):

    for kind, item in _events(data):
        for name, change in _changes(kind, item).items():
            result[name] = result.get(name, Decimal(0)) + change
    return result


def _changes(kind, item):
    changes = {}
    if kind == "expense":
        changes[item["payer"]] = Decimal(item["base_amount"])
        for name, share in item["shares"].items():
            changes[name] = changes.get(name, Decimal(0)) - Decimal(share)
    else:
        amount = Decimal(item["base_amount"])
        changes[item["from"]] = amount
        changes[item["to"]] = -amount
    return changes

    running = Decimal(0)
    rows = []
    for kind, item in _events(data):
        changes = _changes(kind, item)
        if name not in changes:
            continue
        running += changes[name]
        if kind == "expense":
            description = item["description"]
        elif item["from"] == name:
            description = f"Payment to {item['to']}"
        else:
            description = f"Payment from {item['from']}"
        rows.append((item["date"], description, changes[name], running))
    return rows

    Greedily matches the biggest debtor with the biggest creditor, which needs
    at most one payment fewer than the number of people who are not square.
    """
    bal = balances(data)
    creditors = sorted(([n, v] for n, v in bal.items() if v > 0), key=lambda x: (-x[1], x[0]))
    debtors = sorted(([n, -v] for n, v in bal.items() if v < 0), key=lambda x: (-x[1], x[0]))
    payments = []
    i = j = 0
    while i < len(debtors) and j < len(creditors):
        amount = min(debtors[i][1], creditors[j][1])
        payments.append((debtors[i][0], creditors[j][0], amount))
        debtors[i][1] -= amount
        creditors[j][1] -= amount
        if debtors[i][1] == 0:
            i += 1
        if creditors[j][1] == 0:
            j += 1

    totals = {}

        category = totals.setdefault(expense["category"], {})
        for name, share in expense["shares"].items():
            category[name] = category.get(name, Decimal(0)) + Decimal(share)
    order = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(data["members"])}
    return {
        category: dict(sorted(people.items(), key=lambda kv: (order.get(kv[0], len(order)), kv[0])))

    }

import datetime
from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal, InvalidOperation

from kitty.errors import KittyError

CENT = Decimal("0.01")


def _parse_decimal(text, what):
    try:
        value = Decimal(text.strip())
    except (InvalidOperation, AttributeError):
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r} is not a number")
    if not value.is_finite():
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r} is not a number")
    return value


def parse_amount(text, what="amount", allow_zero=False):
    """Parse a money amount: positive (or zero if allowed), at most two decimals."""
    value = _parse_decimal(text, what)
    if value < 0 or (value == 0 and not allow_zero):
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r} must be greater than zero")
    try:
        rounded = value.quantize(CENT)
    except InvalidOperation:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r} is too large")
    if rounded != value:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r} has more than two decimal places")
    return rounded


def parse_weight(text, what):
    """Parse a non-negative number used as a share or percentage."""
    value = _parse_decimal(text, what)
    if value < 0:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r} must not be negative")
    return value


def parse_rate(text):
    value = _parse_decimal(text, "rate")
    if value <= 0:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid rate: {text!r} must be greater than zero")
    return value


def parse_currency(text):
    code = text.strip().upper()
    if len(code) != 3 or not code.isalpha() or not code.isascii():
        raise KittyError(f"invalid currency {text!r}: use a three-letter code such as EUR")
    return code


def parse_date(text):
    try:
        return datetime.datetime.strptime(text.strip(), "%Y-%m-%d").date().isoformat()
    except ValueError:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid date {text!r}: use YYYY-MM-DD")


def to_cents(value):
    return value.quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


def fmt(value):
    """Format money as a string with exactly two decimals (never "-0.00")."""
    value = to_cents(Decimal(value))
    if value == 0:
        value = Decimal("0.00")
    return f"{value:.2f}"


def allocate(total, weights):
    """Split `total` into cents in proportion to `weights`.

    `weights` is a list of (name, weight) pairs. Everyone gets their exact
    portion rounded down to the cent, then the leftover cents go one each to
    people in the order they appear in `weights`, skipping anyone with a zero
    weight. The result adds up to `total` exactly. Zero results are dropped.
    """
    cents = int(to_cents(total) * 100)
    weight_sum = sum(w for _, w in weights)
    if weight_sum <= 0:
        raise KittyError("the split must give a share to at least one person")
    floors = [int(Decimal(cents) * w / weight_sum) for _, w in weights]
    leftover = cents - sum(floors)
    # Leftover is less than the number of people with a non-zero weight,
    # so each of them gets at most one extra cent.
    for i in [i for i, (_, w) in enumerate(weights) if w > 0][:leftover]:
        floors[i] += 1
    return {
        name: Decimal(c).scaleb(-2)
        for (name, _), c in zip(weights, floors)
        if c != 0
    }

"""Calculations over the stored expenses and payments.

def sorted_expenses(data):

def _events(data):
    """Expenses and payments in date order (ties in the order they were added)."""
    events = [(e["date"], 0, e["id"], "expense", e) for e in data["expenses"]]
    events += [(p["date"], 1, p["id"], "payment", p) for p in data["payments"]]

    Greedily matches the biggest debtor with the biggest creditor, which needs
    at most one payment fewer than the number of people who are not square.
    """
    bal = balances(data)

    debtors = sorted(([n, -v] for n, v in bal.items() if v < 0), key=lambda x: (-x[1], x[0]))

import datetime
from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal, InvalidOperation

from kitty.errors import KittyError

CENT = Decimal("0.01")


def _parse_decimal(text, what):
    try:
        value = Decimal(text.strip())
    except (InvalidOperation, AttributeError):
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r} is not a number")
    if not value.is_finite():
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r} is not a number")
    return value


def parse_amount(text, what="amount", allow_zero=False):
    """Parse a money amount: positive (or zero if allowed), at most two decimals."""
    value = _parse_decimal(text, what)
    if value < 0 or (value == 0 and not allow_zero):
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r} must be greater than zero")
    try:
        rounded = value.quantize(CENT)
    except InvalidOperation:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r} is too large")
    if rounded != value:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r} has more than two decimal places")
    return rounded


def parse_weight(text, what):
    """Parse a non-negative number used as a share or percentage."""
    value = _parse_decimal(text, what)
    if value < 0:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r} must not be negative")
    return value


def parse_rate(text):
    value = _parse_decimal(text, "rate")
    if value <= 0:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid rate: {text!r} must be greater than zero")
    return value


def parse_currency(text):
    code = text.strip().upper()
    if len(code) != 3 or not code.isalpha() or not code.isascii():
        raise KittyError(f"invalid currency {text!r}: use a three-letter code such as EUR")
    return code


def parse_date(text):
    try:
        return datetime.datetime.strptime(text.strip(), "%Y-%m-%d").date().isoformat()
    except ValueError:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid date {text!r}: use YYYY-MM-DD")


def to_cents(value):
    return value.quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


def fmt(value):
    """Format money as a string with exactly two decimals (never "-0.00")."""
    value = to_cents(Decimal(value))
    if value == 0:
        value = Decimal("0.00")
    return f"{value:.2f}"


def allocate(total, weights):
    """Split `total` into cents in proportion to `weights`.

    `weights` is a list of (name, weight) pairs. Everyone gets their exact
    portion rounded down to the cent, then the leftover cents go one each to
    people in the order they appear in `weights`, skipping anyone with a zero
    weight. The result adds up to `total` exactly. Zero results are dropped.
    """
    cents = int(to_cents(total) * 100)
    weight_sum = sum(w for _, w in weights)
    if weight_sum <= 0:
        raise KittyError("the split must give a share to at least one person")
    floors = [int(Decimal(cents) * w / weight_sum) for _, w in weights]
    leftover = cents - sum(floors)
    # Leftover is less than the number of people with a non-zero weight,
    # so each of them gets at most one extra cent.
    for i in [i for i, (_, w) in enumerate(weights) if w > 0][:leftover]:
        floors[i] += 1
    return {
        name: Decimal(c).scaleb(-2)
        for (name, _), c in zip(weights, floors)
        if c != 0
    }

        "expenses": [],
        "payments": [],
    }


def exists():
    return os.path.exists(DATA_FILE)


def load():
    if not exists():
        raise KittyError(f"no {DATA_FILE} here; start one with 'python3 -m kitty init EUR'")
    try:
        with open(DATA_FILE, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            data = json.load(f)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        raise KittyError(f"{DATA_FILE} is not valid JSON: {e}")
    except OSError as e:
        raise KittyError(f"cannot read {DATA_FILE}: {e.strerror}")
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or any(
        not isinstance(data.get(key), kind) for key, kind in _REQUIRED.items()
    ):
        raise KittyError(f"{DATA_FILE} does not look like a kitty file")
    return data


def save(data):
    """Write atomically, so an interrupted save never leaves a half-written file."""
    directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(DATA_FILE))
    try:

        try:

                json.dump(data, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
                f.write("\n")

        except BaseException:
            os.unlink(tmp)
            raise
    except OSError as e:
        raise KittyError(f"cannot write {DATA_FILE}: {e.strerror}")

        os.chdir(self._old_cwd)

        """Run a command in-process; returns (status, stdout, stderr)."""
        out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):
            try:
                status = main(list(argv))
            except SystemExit as e:
                status = e.code
        return status, out.getvalue(), err.getvalue()

        status, out, err = self.run_kitty(*argv)
        self.assertEqual(status, 0, f"{argv} failed: {err}")
        return out

        return json.loads(self.ok(*argv))

    def fails(self, *argv, message=""):
        status, out, err = self.run_kitty(*argv)
        self.assertEqual(status, 1, f"{argv} should have failed, got: {out}")
        self.assertIn(message, err)

I've added `expense edit ID` and `--in CUR` for `balances` and `settle`. All 46 tests pass: the 34 that were already there and 12 new ones for these features. The sandbox wouldn't let me create a scratch kitty to try them by hand, so the tests are the only check. They do run each command on a real `kitty.json` in a temporary directory. All the changes are in `kitty/cli.py`, plus the new tests in `tests/test_kitty.py`.

**`expense edit ID`**
- It changes only the options you give. The expense keeps its ID, its place in the list, and its `next_id` slot.
- **Amount or currency changed, no split option:** the expense is split equally among the people in its current shares, in their existing order, so leftover cents go to the same people first.
- **Split option given:** it works exactly like `expense add`, applied to the new amount (or the existing one if you didn't change it). `--exact` must add up to that amount.
- **New currency:** converted at its current rate. If you change only the amount and keep the currency, the expense keeps the rate it was recorded at, so editing an old USD expense doesn't pick up today's rate.
- If you change only the payer, date, description or category, the existing split is left alone, including a custom one.
- Giving `--amount` or `--currency` with the same value as now doesn't count as a change, so it won't undo a custom split.
- Errors are checked the same way as in `expense add`, and nothing is saved if any check fails. One addition: `expense edit 1` with no options at all is an error ("nothing to change").

**`balances --in CUR` / `settle --in CUR`**
- Each amount is converted from the base currency at the current rate, rounded half-up to the cent, with the same JSON as before.
- With the base currency it shows the usual amounts. A currency with no rate gives the existing "no exchange rate for …; set one with …" error.
- Payments are still worked out in the base currency and converted afterwards, so the suggested payments themselves don't change.

**Small refactors:** the ID parsing that `expense remove` used is now shared with `edit`, and `convert` can take a known rate as well as the current one. Neither changes how anything behaves.

**Limitations:**
- "The same people as before" means the people who currently have a share. Someone given a zero share originally, such as `--shares A=0` or a split of a few cents, isn't stored, so they won't be brought back by an equal re-split.
- With `--in`, each balance is rounded on its own, so the converted balances can be a cent off summing to zero. A very strong currency could also show a tiny settle payment as `"0.00"`.
